title: Rapid Credentialing and Evidence Grid — compact
content:
Purpose:
Short working doc to standardize a compact evidence-first path for fast-tracking mid-senior IC hires when time-to-hire is critical (e.g., product launches, critical infra gaps). This is intentionally minimal: keep interviews lean, focus on high-signal probes, and pair with a 30-day shadow-to-certify probation.

Scope:
- Role families: Eng (backend, infra, runtime), Applied ML, Product engineering leads.
- Not intended for executive or highly regulated hires (legal/compliance signoff required).

Core principles (why):
1) Signal over volume — 3 high-quality probes beat 6 generic panels.
2) Evidence first — capture concrete artifacts during interview (PRs, design sketches, runbook excerpts, short take-home code).
3) Shadow probation — hire with a 30-day certification checklist that transfers ownership after proven outcomes.

When to use fast-track (decision rules):
- Role urgent and single contributor shortage AND
- Candidate has >5 years relevant experience with public/verified artifacts OR strong referral + quick technical screener pass.
- Hiring manager signs a fast-track exception form (link above).

Interview format (compact template):
1) 20m Hiring manager intro + scope alignment (must include 1 concrete problem candidate will own).
2) 30m Technical deep-probe (focus: one core system or algorithm).
3) 20m Behavioral + culture fit (STAR, ownership probes).
4) 15m Product/ops thinking or system tradeoffs (role-specific).
5) 15m Practical evidence review (walkthrough of a PR, repo, or mini take-home) — candidate shares screen.
Total: ~100 minutes (+ 10m scheduling buffer).

Compact evidence grid (scoring):
- Each interviewer scores three axes: Technical mastery (0-5), Problem decomposition & communication (0-5), Deliverable evidence (0-5).
- Quick checklist items (Y/N): public repo w/ tests, experience shipping similar feature, infra/runbook ownership, mentorship/IC org contributions.
- Pass threshold: combined score >= 11 with at least a 3 in Deliverable evidence OR manager veto override with documented remediation plan.

Example scoring table (for notes):
- Int1 (HM): Tech 4, Comm 4, Evidence 3 => 11
- Int2 (Peer): Tech 3, Comm 4, Evidence 2 => 9
- Int3 (SRE/Infra): Tech 4, Comm 3, Evidence 3 => 10
Sum = 30 -> pass (>=11 average across three interviewers).

Scoring guidance (calibration notes):
- Technical mastery: assess depth on relevant component rather than breadth. Favor deep implementation details, tradeoffs, and debugging stories.
- Problem decomposition: look for explicit assumptions, edge cases, and measurable success criteria.
- Deliverable evidence: scoring favors shipped work (links, release notes), not just theoretical discussion. If candidate lacks public artifacts, require a short paired task in week 1 of probation.

Behavioral probes (compact prompts):
- Ownership probe: "Tell me about a time you owned a system that failed in production. What did you do, how did you prioritize, and what changed afterward?"
- Influence probe: "Describe a cross-team decision you led where the right engineering choice was not obvious."
- Mentorship probe: "Give an example of how you helped a teammate unblock on a tricky infra or design problem."

Technical deep-probe examples (pick one):
- Backend/Infra: design a cache invalidation strategy for a low-latency model KV store; discuss consistency, eviction, instrumentation, and rollbacks.
- Applied ML: propose an eval/metric strategy for model regression detection in streaming traffic; include sample prompts, dataset slicing, and alerting thresholds.
- Runtime: walk through optimizing KV cache locality across GPUs; what metrics, what kernel-level tradeoffs, what regression risks?

Practical evidence review (what to ask during repo walkthrough):
- Which commits show ownership? Which tests cover core logic? Are there CI artifacts or perf benchmarks?
- Ask candidate to point to a specific bug they fixed and describe the repro, the fix, and the rollout plan.

Fast-track offer conditions (probation):
- Role-specific 30-day certification checklist appended to offer: 5 measurable outcomes (e.g., ship a bugfix with tests and perf measurement; onboard a peer to run the service; deliver a runbook).
- Weekly syncs during probation: hiring manager + mentor + people-ops buddy.
- Failed certification: 2-week transition/remediation plan OR termination (depending on severity).

Onboarding checkpoints (compact 0-30 days):
- Day0: account provisioning + security training + key contacts list.
- Day1: product demo + team 30m intro + first small bug assignment.
- Week1: paired PR with reviewer; demo of infra pipelines; pass access checklist.
- Week2: deliver first measurable task (bugfix or small feature) with test coverage and perf note.
- Week4: certification review; evaluate against 30-day checklist; decision: certify / extend / remediate.

Artifacts to collect at offer stage (people-ops):
- Signed fast-track exception approval (manager + People Ops)
- Candidate evidence pack (links to repos, PRs, references)
- Proposed 30-day certification checklist (3-5 items)

Open questions & TODOs:
- Decide whether to surface coding exercise for roles with lower public artifact density (e.g., applied ML without open repos). Proposal: short 2-hour paired task in week 1 instead of pre-hire take-home.
- Legal: confirm probation language is compatible with regional labor laws (APAC). Assigned: Marisol.
- Ops: create a fast-track offer template for recruiters to use (GH PR open).

Calibration notes for people-ops:
- Run monthly 30-min calibration with hiring managers that used fast-track last month; capture false-positive hires and process fixes.
- Keep fast-track usage under 10% of total hires per quarter unless exec signoff.

Appendix: quick templates (copy/paste)
- Fast-track approval (one-liner): "Hiring manager requests fast-track for [role] due to [reason]. Candidate: [name]. Evidence: [links]. People Ops approval: [name/date]."
- 30-day checklist example: "1) ship PR with tests (owner: candidate), 2) reduce critical issue backlog by triage (owner: candidate), 3) demo system to peer group, 4) runbook authored and reviewed, 5) mentor onboarding session led."

Notes to self: keep this doc short and iterate after 2 hires. Capture anonymized learnings in /hr/hiring-retrospectives (Confluence).

---
History: created as an experiment by Asha K. after Q3 infra hiring crunch. Intend to surface to TA and Eng leads for pilot January 2026.
